pairs.why: B's locomotive has a working cowcatcher grille, connecting rods linking the wheels, and a coal tender behind the cab, while A's front is a solid slab plow with a cab block stuck on top and little drive linkage.
B's wagon has a hitching pole and its canvas opening at the front, but A's canvas has a round hole cut in the side and no usable pole.
A's rocket has a riveted exhaust nozzle that the flame comes out of and fins mounted on the body, while B's fins sit loosely at the base around a plain black ring.
B's director-style chair has X-braces on the front and side that clearly hold up the seat and armrests, while in A it's hard to tell how the back posts connect to the X-legs and bottom frame.
B's lifebuoy and rope coil hang on posts that hold up the deck, while A's lifebuoy reflection shows up far away in open water, not under the ring.
A's calculator has labeled digit and operator keys, a screen and a solar strip like the real card, while B's keys are blank so it could not be used.
A's lasso loop runs out of the tied coil through a knotted eye, while B's loop joins the coil at a meaningless white band and its rope ends tangle into the coil.
B's cat sits on all four paws with its tail rising behind its body, while A's tail flops forward from the floor and its head and ears look stuck on.
